title: Legislative districts of Zamboanga Sibugay
wikitext:
{{Short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Zamboanga Sibugay''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Zamboanga Sibugay]] in the [[Congress of the Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the Congress through its [[#1st District|first]] and [[#2nd District|second]] congressional districts. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Mindanao and Sulu|Legislative district of Zamboanga|Legislative district of Zamboanga del Sur}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Zamboanga Sibugay were represented under the [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]] (1917–1935), the historical [[Zamboanga (province)|Zamboanga Province]] (1935–1953), [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region IX]] (1978–1984) and [[Zamboanga del Sur]] (1953–1972; 1984–2001). The passage of Republic Act No. 8973 on November 7, 2000, and its subsequent ratification by plebiscite on February 22, 2001, separated the entire [[Legislative districts of Zamboanga del Sur#3rd District (defunct)|third district]] of [[Zamboanga del Sur]] to form the new province of [[Zamboanga Sibugay]].{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 8973 - An Act Creating the Province of Zamboanga Sibugay from the Province of Zamboanga del Sur and for Other Purposes|url=http://www.thecorpusjuris.com/legislative/republic-acts/ra-no-8973.php|author=Congress of the Philippines|date=November 7, 2000|website=The Corpus Juris|access-date=November 27, 2017}} Zamboanga del Sur's former third district automatically became the representation of [[Zamboanga Sibugay]] upon its establishment in February 2001, but the new province only elected a representative under its own name beginning in the [[2001 Philippine House of Representatives elections|May 2001 elections]]. The enactment of Republic Act No. 9360 on October 26, 2006, increased Zamboanga Sibugay's representation by reapportioning the province into two congressional districts,{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 9360 - An Act Creating Another Congressional District in the Province of Zamboanga Sibugay, Amending for the Purpose Republic Act Numbered Eighty-Nine Hundred and Seventy-Three, otherwise known as The Charter of the Province of Zamboanga Sibugay|url=http://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2006/ra_9360_2006.html|author=Congress of the Philippines|date=October 26, 2006|website=The LawPhil Project|access-date=February 4, 2017}} which began to elect their separate representatives in the [[2007 Philippine House of Representatives elections|2007 elections]]. == Current districts == Zamboanga Sibugay's current congressional delegation is composed of two members. {{Color box|{{party color|Partido Federal ng Pilipinas}}|border=darkgray}} [[Partido Federal ng Pilipinas|PFP]] (2) {| class="wikitable sortable" style="margin: 1em auto; font-size:100%; line-height:20px; text-align:center" |+Legislative districts and representatives of [[Zamboanga Sibugay]] ! rowspan="2" |District ! colspan="3" |Current Representative ! rowspan="2" |Party ! rowspan="2" |Constituent [[Local government in the Philippines|LGUs]] ! rowspan="2" |Population (2020){{PH census|2020|01}} ! rowspan="2" |Area{{Cite web |title=List of Provinces |url=http://www.nscb.gov.ph/activestats/psgc/listprov.asp |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160419000512/http://www.nscb.gov.ph/activestats/psgc/listprov.asp |archive-date=April 19, 2016 |access-date=August 2, 2022 |website=PSGC Interactive |publisher=National Statistical Coordination Board}} ! rowspan="2" |Map |- ! colspan="2" |Image !Name |- ![[Zamboanga Sibugay's 1st congressional district|1st]] | style="background:{{party color|Partido Federal ng Pilipinas}};" | | [[File:Rep.
